title: Delegation refresh consumes parent waits and queues resume prompts in memory before its commit; a commit failure loses them
outcome: A delegation terminal refresh whose commit fails leaves every registered parent wait and its resume prompt retained or durably owned, never consumed only in memory.
acceptance: When the commit in refresh_delegation_for_child_session fails after the delegation was mutated, the parent waits it took are restored and the resume prompts it queued in memory are removed, or a volatile duty owned by the retry tick retains them until a later commit succeeds; no wait is consumed without a successful commit.

A fail-first test injects a commit failure at that point on a delegation terminal path and shows, on the frozen pre-fix tree, the wait consumed with no durable record; after the fix the wait is retained (or durably owned) and the parent is woken exactly once when the commit later succeeds.
Regression controls show healthy delegation terminal paths (completed, failed, cancelled) still consume their waits once and wake the parent once.
